newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania takes in 56 percent of wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Romania takes in 56 percent of wheat crop.

text.p: Romania has taken in more than half its 1997 wheat crop, but harvesting of the expected bumper crop has been delayed by recent rains, the farming ministry said on Friday.
Ministry figures show yields exceeded initial estimates, with 4.250 million tonnes of wheat harvested, or 56 percent of 2.38 million hectares under that crop.
This was up from 3.226 million tonnes a week ago.
Average yield per hectare was 3,142 kg, higher than initial estimates of 2,963, the data showed.
The ministry expects a total wheat crop of 7.07 million tonnes, almost double the level last year while exports are seen at over two million tonnes.
Ministry officials said delays in wheat harvesting, which should have been completed by end July, were due to rain which affected most of the Balkan country over the past weeks.
But they denied suggestions that bad weather affecting most of eastern Europe could have an impact on the crop.
Data issued by the Environment Ministry's flood commission on Friday showed that 10,000 hectares of crop land had been submerged during the past week, especially in western Romania.
But the floods have not affected the main granaries in southern and central Romania.
There was no breakdown by crops of the areas under water.
The farming ministry said it would issue new crop data in mid-August.

Of the wheat harvested so far, 1.203 million tonnes had been supplied to the consumption and fodder fund, a ministry press official said. Farmers held another 2.928 million tonnes, with 120,000 tonnes of wheat taken in for seed.
